title: The Orion Nebula and cluster from the VLT Survey Telescope
caption: The Orion Nebula and its star cluster, imaged by ESO's VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: Ranked #24 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This detailed view shows the Orion Nebula together with its cluster of young stars, captured by OmegaCAM, the wide-field optical camera on ESO's VLT Survey Telescope.

The Orion Nebula is a famous object and the birthplace of many massive stars. At a distance of about 1350 light-years, it counts among the nearest stellar nurseries. A stellar nursery is a cloud of gas and dust in which new stars are taking shape, and the energy from the young stars lights up the surrounding gas.

The cluster and the nebula belong together. The stars formed from the cloud, and their radiation now shapes and illuminates what remains of it. OmegaCAM's wide field lets both fit in one frame. The picture was taken through filters spanning visible light and the near-infrared, including one tuned to the red glow of hydrogen. The official caption offers little more detail.
scale: The nebula lies about 1350 light-years away, according to ESO.

understand.summary: This image comes from OmegaCAM on the VLT Survey Telescope, using visible and near-infrared filters plus one for hydrogen light. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
filters: 480 nm · Optical G (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
625 nm · Optical r (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
659 nm · Optical H-alpha (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
770 nm · Optical i (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared, which the eye cannot see, and long exposures bring out faint gas that would be invisible by eye.
